_theme_note: Optional. Any CSS custom property from deck.html can be overridden here, so one content file can render in a different brand without touching the template.
_cuts_note: Same content, different decks. List slide ids in the order you want them. Build with --cut investor. Slides without an id can never appear in a cut, which is a useful way to keep a slide in the long deck only.
_text_note: Wrap a phrase in ~tildes~ to colour it with the accent. Keeps markup out of the copy.

slides.title:
One clear claim.
~Stated plainly.~
slides.sub: A single sentence that says what this is and who it is for. Resist the urge to add a second.

items.title: The cost today
items.body: One concrete, checkable number beats three adjectives. Say where it comes from.

items.title: The delay today
items.body: Keep each card to one idea. If it needs a comma-spliced sentence, it is two cards.

items.title: The gap today
items.body: Numbers in the alert colour read as the cost of the status quo.

slides.title: The mechanism, ~in four steps~

items.body: A headline number that proves the mechanism, with the measurement conditions stated.
A second number, ideally one a sceptic would ask for next.

slides.kicker: One line that lands the point of the slide.

items.title: Capability
items.body: One sentence. Concrete verb, no adjectives.

items.title: Capability
items.body: If two capabilities need the same sentence, cut one.

items.title: Capability
items.body: Six is the most a reader will take in at a glance.

items.title: Capability
items.body: Name the thing the way users say it, not the internal name.

items.title: Capability
items.body: Prefer what it does over how it is built.

items.title: Capability
items.body: Leave the rest for the appendix.

slides.title: How we ~compare~
slides.kicker: Prefix a cell with + for accent, - for alert. Be fair; a comparison that flatters you everywhere reads as marketing.

slides.quote: A real sentence someone said, that a prospect would ~recognise as their own problem~.

slides.title:
The one thing you want
them to ~do next.~
slides.sub: Make the ask specific. 'Book a technical deep dive' beats 'get in touch'.
